known facts:
if seed%2 == 0:
    male
else:
    female
if seed%10 == 0:
    beard


hair study:
it seems to repeat in a pattern of 7 in order, briefly ignoring gender during picking the index
(this is the thing that made me want to study every behavior)
these are all the hairs sorted based on when they show up
male = {"Charmer","Cool","Dev","Dreamy","Popstar","Neat","Spiky","Shaggy","MessyWavy","Fluffed"}
female = {"Animazing","Anime","Bob","Drama","Cropped","Wild","Classic","Long","Ponytail","Wolfish","Wavy","Short"}

seed 0-7 -> Charmer/Animazing depending on gender picked
seed 8-14 -> Cool/Anime
seed 15-21 -> Dev/Bob
...all predictions should follow a pattern of 7 (they also repeat after table runs out, tables being independent), deducing:

hair = gender[floor(seed/7)%#gender+1]

(gender being male/female depending on the known facts above)
(reminder that lua starts from 1 instead of 0 for table indexing, reason for the +1 inside)


beard study:
i assumed it is the exact same as the hair but with one smaller pool and i was kinda right
beards = {"Neat","Thin","Trimmed"}
its kind of hard to do due to how few they actually are during testing, especially because i am sure they dont get calculated only when they appear
so i used another row with only multiples of 10
noting that since the seed is a multiple of 10 that means it is also even by design, so bearded npcs are always male
(i tried spawning BasicSecurityLead1 but that only sets thin beard, does not care about the beard check)

seed 0 -> Neat
seed 10 -> Trimmed
seed 20 -> Thin
seed 30 -> Neat
seed 40 -> Trimmed
seed 50 -> Thin
..pattern repeats this way

now i am pretty sure it follows the same principle as the hair because it is probably autogenerated
so i will still assume that principle (and also that non multiples of 10 technically get assigned their own even if discarded) for the calculation

-- (this is me from the future, i did it like this because for some reason i was convinced hair was sorted alphabetically (??), wish i knew why)

after like a couple minutes of bruteforcing this looks like the most accurate so far

beard = beards[floor(seed/5)%#beards+1]

this checks out as:
seed X-0 -> Neat (shown)
seed 1-5 -> Thin
seed 6-10 -> Trimmed (shown)
seed 11-15 -> Neat
seed 16-20 -> Thin (shown)
seed 21-25 -> Trimmed
seed 26-30 -> Neat (shown)
seed 31-35 -> Thin
seed 36-40 -> Trimmed (shown)
seed 41-45 -> Neat
seed 46-50 -> Thin (shown)
seed 51-55 -> Trimmed

(also im really sorry if i mix up python syntax with luau throughout this please bear with me its just a small raw research)
would have been easier to swap out the entries in the table but i wanted to be accurate i guess (i wasted so much time)

-- (this is me from the future, indeed i have as this could also not be the right order, but it works so whatever)

...then repeats the pattern, exactly 100 seeds each time, deducing:

if seed%100 < 15:
    ethnicity = "black"
elif seed%100 < 30:
    ethnicity = "beige"
elif seed%100 < 70:
    ethnicity = "white"
elif seed%100 < 85:
    ethnicity = "tan"
else:
    ethnicity = "medium"
skincolor = skincolors[ethnicity][floor(seed/3)%#skincolors[ethnicity]+1]

im still convinced theres probably some deducible order like the rest but i just dont know what their names could be

hair color study:
also incredibly odd? took me a WHILE to figure out on a separate sheet, will reconstruct thought process here:
i got these colors from the lobby and checked out which ones appeared and which didnt, in order as usual
lobbypicked = {
    {90,76,66},
    {135,79,44},
    {27,42,53},
}
but there seem to be more as far as i could tell, adding up to:
local haircolors = {
    {27,42,53},--13
    {52,52,52},--2
    {86,66,54},--11
    {57,43,35},--4
    {99,95,98},--9
    {199,172,120},--13
    {90,76,66},--13
    {135,79,44},--5
    --cycle repeats a bit and then here is other colors:
    {33,33,33},
    {30,22,18},
    {124,92,70},
}
(tested through an albino filter with perfect conditions and darkest samples)
(needless to say they may not be perfect even after rigorous testing on my side of things by switching rgb values)
the thing is, upon observing further i was able to link up the fact that the specific pool is tied to ethnicity
black people only have black hair and can have darker shades than others, while white people have the most choices

the pool seems to be 13 after careful considerations in the pattern (the --n on every entry in the table was added now)
if it is it would also explain the prior skin color theory
